headline: Diplomacy: Bangladesh maintains 'unique' relations with all countries, says Shama Obaed
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed emphasizes national interest and explores new Chinese investments and economic corridors.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam described Bangladesh's diplomatic ties with all nations as "unique," stating that the goal is to protect the country's interests through good relations.
Addressing reporters at the foreign ministry, she clarified that maintaining strong ties with one country does not mean ties with another will be compromised.
The minister expressed optimism that a recent state visit to China will lead to increased Chinese investment in Bangladesh.
She noted that China's proposals are being reviewed and will be implemented if they serve the interests of the Bangladeshi people.
Regarding the Teesta River barrage project, Shama Obaed stated that the feasibility study will resume from where it was stopped, with China providing technical support.
Bangladesh is also examining a proposed "economic corridor" from China via Myanmar, which the government welcomes as a boost for trade and the economy.
On a separate note, the state minister mentioned that there has been no progress in the process of returning former prime minister Sheikh Hasina to face trial.
caption:
Bangladesh's diplomatic strategy: 'Unique' relations with all, focused on national interest.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam described Bangladesh's diplomatic ties with all nations as "unique," stating that the goal is to protect the country's interests through good relations.

Addressing reporters at the foreign ministry, she clarified that maintaining strong ties with one country does not mean ties with another will be compromised.

The minister expressed optimism that a recent state visit to China will lead to increased Chinese investment in Bangladesh.

She noted that China's proposals are being reviewed and will be implemented if they serve the interests of the Bangladeshi people.

Regarding the Teesta River barrage project, Shama Obaed stated that the feasibility study will resume from where it was stopped, with China providing technical support.

Bangladesh is also examining a proposed "economic corridor" from China via Myanmar, which the government welcomes as a boost for trade and the economy.

On a separate note, the state minister mentioned that there has been no progress in the process of returning former prime minister Sheikh Hasina to face trial.

headline_marked: ACC [[seeks records from Bangladesh Bank]] in probe against 3 ex-governors
headline: ACC seeks records from Bangladesh Bank in probe against 3 ex-governors
summary: The anti-graft watchdog is investigating allegations of abuse of authority and policies favoring loan defaulters and influential business groups.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has requested additional documents from Bangladesh Bank to investigate allegations against former governors Atiur Rahman, Fazle Kabir, and Abdur Rouf Talukder.
In a letter sent on June 11, the ACC demanded that the central bank submit the required records by June 30.
The probe focuses on allegations that key officials abused their authority to issue policies favoring loan defaulters and influential business groups, including the S Alam Group.
The ACC is seeking certified copies of approvals issued in 2016 and between 2020-2024 regarding the Single Borrower Exposure Limit and large loan rescheduling.
Additional requests include documents on board members from 2009 to 2024, companies that received incentive loans, and approvals allowing S Alam Group to acquire bank ownership.
The commission is also investigating approvals issued during Abdur Rouf Talukder's tenure regarding printing money to provide liquidity support to banks owned by the S Alam Group.
The ACC is currently reviewing documents already received from the central bank and will issue further reminders if the information is found to be incomplete.
caption:
Three former Bangladesh Bank governors are under investigation by the ACC for alleged abuse of authority.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has requested additional documents from Bangladesh Bank to investigate allegations against former governors Atiur Rahman, Fazle Kabir, and Abdur Rouf Talukder.

In a letter sent on June 11, the ACC demanded that the central bank submit the required records by June 30.

The probe focuses on allegations that key officials abused their authority to issue policies favoring loan defaulters and influential business groups, including the S Alam Group.

The ACC is seeking certified copies of approvals issued in 2016 and between 2020-2024 regarding the Single Borrower Exposure Limit and large loan rescheduling.

Additional requests include documents on board members from 2009 to 2024, companies that received incentive loans, and approvals allowing S Alam Group to acquire bank ownership.

The commission is also investigating approvals issued during Abdur Rouf Talukder's tenure regarding printing money to provide liquidity support to banks owned by the S Alam Group.

The ACC is currently reviewing documents already received from the central bank and will issue further reminders if the information is found to be incomplete.
